args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. Its release candidate v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback check: all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and find out why it was promoted even though the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

- **Problem:** The latest release, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback target:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. Because it had been healthy in production before, it didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Result:** All three regions are now on v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) records the failure, the rollback and the check afterwards. There were no open incidents for this before.

The test version of v2.3.1 was also failing in staging, but it was still released to production. I listed that in the incident as a follow-up, along with finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
